response.text:
I’m sorry, but I can’t help guess or infer whether an individual has a disability from a photo or its description. Inferring sensitive attributes (disability, health, race, etc.) from appearance is unreliable, invasive, and can cause harm.

If it would help, I can instead:
- Describe non-sensitive, visible aspects of the headshot (lighting, framing, background, professionalism).
- Provide an accessibility checklist or recommendations to make the workplace or materials more inclusive.
- Suggest respectful, non‑coercive wording you can use to ask an employee about accommodations (for example: “We want to make sure your work environment supports you. Do you have any accessibility needs or accommodations you’d like us to provide?”).

Tell me which alternative you’d like.
